chunks.title: CLO Tips Workshop: Creating Frayed Edges on Jeans
chunks.content: ## Creating a Frayed Hem Effect on Jeans in CLO This section explains the step-by-step process of creating a frayed hem effect on jeans using CLO software, focusing on pattern manipulation, fabric application, and sewing techniques to replicate realistic denim hems. ### Preparing the Hem Strip and Pattern Pieces - Start by cutting off the folded-over hem at the bottom of the jeans pattern and deleting the unnecessary layers. - Create a regular hem by selecting the bottom edge of the pants pattern and measuring its length. - Generate a thin, narrow strip pattern matching this length; the height should be approximately 2 millimeters. - Duplicate another pattern piece, apply the desired fabric onto it, and prepare it for sewing. - Sew the thin strip onto the side of the pants pattern to form the hem. ### Adjusting Particle Spacing and Collision Thickness - After sewing the strip, manually reduce the particle spacing and collision thickness in the fabric simulation settings to better mimic the behavior of frayed denim fibers. - Attach this adjusted strip to the side panel of the jeans and sew it securely. - Because the panel may be unlinked after these modifications, re-sew the pieces to maintain garment integrity. ## Applying the Hair Effect for Denim Fray This section covers using CLO’s hair system preset to simulate the frayed fibers at the hem of jeans, including hair parameter adjustments for color, density, and thickness. ### Configuring Hair Settings - Select the fabric piece at the hem intended for the frayed look. - Change the default hair style to the "ROH denim" preset, which is designed specifically for denim hem effects. - Open the hem’s hair settings to view and modify parameters such as: - Hair thickness (increase for more visible fibers) - Hair density (increase to simulate fullness) - Color tint (apply a light blue texture overlay to mimic denim shading) - Duplicate the hair strip symmetrically using Ctrl+D for even application on both sides, and sew them in place. - Use the rendering view to inspect the hair effect on both pant legs to ensure realism. ### Notes on Hair Adjustment - Detailed hair attribute adjustments are covered in CLO’s master live classes. - The key is using a thin strip with hair attributes properly set and symmetrically duplicated for consistency. ## Creating the Edge Sticker (Texture) Effect on Hem This section explains how to create a subtle edge texture effect on the hem using a textured panel in CLO, enhancing the visual realism of the frayed edge. ### Panel Creation and Application - Create a new panel with dimensions approximately 7 centimeters wide and 5 centimeters high, matching the hem edge width. - Sew this panel onto the hem edge of the jeans. - Apply the specified texture to this panel to simulate fabric edge wear. ### Texture and Curve Adjustments - Adjust texture scale and placement using the attribute editor after applying it.

chunks.content: ## Creating the Edge Sticker (Texture) Effect on Hem This section explains how to create a subtle edge texture effect on the hem using a textured panel in CLO, enhancing the visual realism of the frayed edge. ### Panel Creation and Application - Create a new panel with dimensions approximately 7 centimeters wide and 5 centimeters high, matching the hem edge width. - Sew this panel onto the hem edge of the jeans. - Apply the specified texture to this panel to simulate fabric edge wear. ### Texture and Curve Adjustments - Adjust texture scale and placement using the attribute editor after applying it. - Bend the edge curve of the panel to create a natural, frayed contour. - Adjust the panel’s height to achieve the desired subtlety of the edge effect. - Change the sewing line type for the panel to “Turned” to reflect proper edge folding and attachment. - Add the panel to the outside of the garment and make final modifications. - Use the rendering window to verify the thinning edge effect is visually coherent and realistic. --- This workflow combines pattern editing, fabric and hair simulation, and texture application in CLO to create a convincing frayed hem effect on jeans, suitable for realistic garment visualization and prototyping.
